title: Why Your Amazon Product Photos Look Amateur (Even When You Follow the Rules)
description: Following Amazon's rules but still looking amateur? Here's what separates professional-looking listings from technically-compliant ones.

blocks.text: Amazon's image rules are simple. Pure white background. 85% product frame. No watermarks. Easy.
But you can follow every rule and still look amateur next to top listings. Why?
The Rule-Compliance Trap
Amazon's rules define the floor, not the ceiling. Every serious seller meets the rules. Then top sellers do things beyond the rules that separate them.
Here's what those things are.
Difference 1: Lighting Direction
Amateur listings: Light coming from random directions across catalog. Some products lit from top, some from side, some from front.
Professional listings: Consistent lighting direction across every product in the catalog.
Fix: Standardize your shooting setup. Even fix inconsistent lighting during editing at edit-photo.com.
Difference 2: Product Positioning
Amateur listings: Product centered but slightly off, sometimes rotated randomly.
Professional listings: Precise centering, consistent angle across all photos.
Use a dedicated crop or layout editor for exact framing, then use edit-photo for background removal and edge review.
Difference 3: Edge Cleanup
Amateur listings: Fuzzy edges from background removal, occasional artifacts.
Professional listings: Perfect edges even on complex products.
Fix: edit-photo.com's AI handles edges better than manual work. Zoom to 100% and inspect—clean up any remaining artifacts.
Difference 4: Shadow Consistency
Amateur listings: Mixed shadow styles. Some with, some without.
Professional listings: Consistent shadow presence and style.
Note: Amazon main images can't have shadows. Secondary images can. Standardize the secondary shadows.
Difference 5: Color Grading
Amateur listings: Slightly different white balance across photos. Some warm, some cool.
Professional listings: Every photo feels part of the same shoot.
Fix: Edit in batches at edit-photo.com with identical settings.
Difference 6: Resolution
Amateur listings: 1000x1000 (Amazon minimum).
Professional listings: 2500x2500+ (enables zoom feature).
Fix: Always export at maximum available resolution.
Difference 7: Additional Images
Amateur listings: 4-5 photos maximum, sparse.
Professional listings: 9 photos filled, each with a distinct purpose.
Fix: Plan your 9-image sequence. Main image, angles, details, lifestyle, spec callouts, comparisons, size reference, package shot, guarantee.
Difference 8: Enhanced Brand Content
Amateur brands: No EBC. Just standard listing.
Professional brands: Full A+ Content with brand story, comparison charts, feature callouts.
Fix: Register your brand, unlock EBC, use transparent PNGs from edit-photo.com to build EBC modules.
The Cumulative Effect
Each difference alone is minor. Combined, they're the difference between "another Amazon seller" and "obvious top-tier brand."
Buyers can't articulate what's different. They just trust one more than the other.
The Fix Timeline

items.text: Use edit-photo to remove the background and export a transparent PNG. Create white or branded layout versions with the site's supported main-image workflow or a separate design editor; capture and color correction still need to be handled before or after background removal.
Week 2: Fix edges and color consistency
Week 3: Expand from 4-5 photos to full 9-photo sets

blocks.text: One month. Amateur → professional.
